fact: The 'lonely star' of the southern autumn sky — a young star girdled by a sharp-edged ring of debris.
bio: Fomalhaut (Alpha Piscis Austrini) is a hot white star about 25 light-years away, one of the brightest in the sky and conspicuously isolated from other bright stars. It is encircled by a striking dusty debris ring, sculpted by unseen gravity — one of the first such rings ever imaged in visible light.
cultural: Its name comes from the Arabic for 'mouth of the [southern] fish'. One of the four ancient Persian 'Royal Stars', Fomalhaut was a marker of the season and a waypoint for navigators of the southern horizon.
